_comment: Dimensional Infiltrator converts mana into a DECK-OUT: '{1}{C}: Target opponent exiles the
top card of their library.' No {T} and no sacrifice, so it is repeatable within one turn and
bounded only by mana -- which is what makes it a win condition rather than a slow drip.
Three cards left in their library and six mana of which four are colourless: exactly three
activations, so the library empties THIS turn and the win turn is this turn (their draw at the
end of it is the loss, CR 104.3c; the user's rule is that a decked opponent's win turn is OUR
last turn, since they never get a main phase).
This exercises the whole chain end to end -- the ModeSpec enumeration, the searched activation
COUNT axis, the plan-signature fold that keeps three activations from deduping down to one,
the apply loop that pays activations 2 and 3 out of the turn's real mana, opponentdeck's mill
primitive, and the deck-out win check. The opponent is at FULL life, so nothing here can be
confused with a damage kill: they end on 18 life, i.e. the 2 the Infiltrator's body hit for in combat, nowhere near lethal. The win is the empty library.
